rows.what the ink shows: Several enclosed oval returns surround a long stem that descends and curls left; despite heavy retracing, the closed loop-and-descender structure supports varphi.
An initial short descending stroke and upper hook survive, but the horizontal cancellation runs through the following low bodies; a and r cannot be separated securely.
The raised insertion has a looped d, a detached apostrophe and two low following bodies ending in a short sloping stroke; these support d’où, though the compressed vowels limit confidence.
The first word is covered by a thick doubled horizontal cancellation. In the second, the looped d, separate i dot and later upright t remain visible, allowing directe to be recovered.
The insertion begins with a deep p-shaped return and continues through a small upright d loop to a hooked terminal t; the low connecting letters are compressed.
The subscript has a broad upper hook, a thick descending middle and a distinct rightward lower foot. That stepped outline favors 2 over the short triangular 1 in the following A subscript.

After the low initial body, an isolated middle stroke descends deeply below the writing line and the final rising run ends in a crossed t. Those features favor ayant over muni, which would require a final dotted i.
The first separate group has a narrow looped d with a long low e exit; after a clear gap, the second group shows shallow connected u/n shoulders.

The crossed first word retains a large open C and high l; the following p descends through the strike and the final q has its own lower return. The connecting bodies remain partially visible under the cancellation.

The initial l loop, apostrophe, g descender and b upright identify l’algèbre; de ses and the two p descenders of propres remain traceable. In éléments the long middle run is crossed and flattened, leaving too few separate letter bodies for a secure full recovery.

Between the quotation marks, a p descender, the small looped upright of d and the final t stem survive the horizontal strike. Their ordered positions support produit despite the flattened connecting strokes.

The separated low au and sens groups lead to looped des, then p, d and crossed t in produit. The final t has a broad return, but no separable final s can be distinguished from that return and the nearby cancellation.

The second word retains the high l, descending g loop and later b upright of algèbres. The first shows a d-like loop and short tail with a detached mark, but lacks the distinct crossed x visible in the page’s earlier deux.

The capital A has clear sloping sides and a looped lower return. Its lower-right index curls down beside a separate upper dot while cancellation crosses the join, so 1 cannot be securely distinguished from an i-like index.
A low horizontal e/s group ends in a separate angular rising t; the cancellation lies above these surviving strokes.
The struck word retains an initial i and dot, a small looped d ascender near its middle, and the upright hooked final t. The intervening low bodies merge with the deletion line.

The cancelled word preserves the tall initial f, the raised middle t and the low terminal hooked group. The same page’s clear facteur has the corresponding f–t spacing, although cancellation conceals most small counters here.

The raised insertion has a long downstroke ending in a small shoulder, then a dot and detached terminal bar. Its o/m/b bodies cannot be separated securely from the horizontal ink above, so the full word versus a contraction remains unsettled.
Above the deleted line, a small initial oval is followed by a tall l and a rounded terminal r/s sweep. The insertion arrow remains separate beneath the letters.
After the cancelled E est, the initial open c and low e connection survive, followed by a prominent crossed angular t. The long cancellation merges with the lower letter bodies.
The compressed word retains its initial rising a/l stroke, the closed descending g loop, an accent above, and a second raised b stroke before the trailing re line.

The insertion shows the separated short auto group, then an a loop, a tall d, a downward j turn and a long terminal ointe connection ending in a pointed t. Its curved insertion line runs below rather than through those letters.
Despite the strike-through, the initial o/n loop, the a loop and dotted i of sait, its tall crossed t, and the long q descender of que remain in sequence.

The phrase starts with a descending q and separated i-dot, followed by the short se group. The next compact group retains a dotted middle stroke, and the final long nécessairement group ends in the writer’s angular t; the small interior letters are compressed.

The fresh enlargement shows a shallow open left cup rising into a small shoulder, then a nearly horizontal right tail. There is neither a closed rho head nor its descending stem; the compressed cup and tail still do not securely distinguish mu from nu.

The deleted segment preserves an initial A-like slant with a dot/dash group, then a tall l-like upright and a low right curl. The heavy stroke removes the word bodies, so even the possible Ainsi le recovery is not secure.

The deleted phrase retains the low de group, the tall t and lower return in type, an isolated upright I with a foot, and the tall p followed by a low ur connection. Several cancellation strokes cross the small bodies but leave those spaced components visible.
The initial tall triangular A, the later dotted i stroke, a small rounded on group and the terminal short a-like upturn survive along the cancellation. The low n/s connections are partly covered.
A capital D retains its upright and rounded bowl; after the flattened e, the p descends below the strike and the l rises above the connected low us strokes.

The initial A, small nsi strokes and comma are visible, followed by the descending p, q and short la group. Several crossing lines merge the bodies of the final two words, so their full sequence remains uncertain.

Ainsi has a distinct capital A and compact trailing strokes, followed by a separated low en group. The last word preserves the tall d, deep returning f stroke and raised terminal t connection despite its compressed middle.
The inserted word begins with an open c curve, then a small o and connected low humps, ending in a long rising-and-returning e stroke before the separate underlined c.
The canceled symbol has a tall sloping stem joined to a closed lower bowl, with a separate short underline below; the crossing line cuts the bowl without removing its outline.
A left upward hook and a terminal raised hook remain above a broad horizontal cancellation. The intervening body is merged with that line, preventing a secure distinction of the proposed d and e.

The first word retains its open c and an upright near its end, but the central letters are buried in the strike. The following d loop and ascender, separated ans traces and two low connected humps of un remain legible.
The measure symbol is reduced to a tiny upright opening hook followed by a nearly flat right stroke. It shows neither a secure closed rho bowl nor a separately identifiable second mu shoulder.

After i and the two-bar membership sign, the final character is one tall left-bowed curve with a lower hook, separate middle bar and detached upper-right oblique mark. It differs from the two-legged Omega later on this line, but the C/E distinction remains unresolved.
Within the first braces, a separate dot stands above a short stem with a hooked base; it is not the undotted tall t seen in nearby words.
The second braced index also has a detached dot above its short stem. The heavily closed lower hook could resemble another letter by itself, but its dotted upper structure supports i.

Above and around the cancellation, the first group preserves its loop, long low connection and separate i dot; the next has a curved s and an end t hook. The final des remains at the right with a raised loop and short terminal sweep.
The initial f is crossed by the vertical paragraph cancellation, but the following connected act strokes retain a raised crossed t. The low rounded eurs sequence runs into the closing parenthesis.

The word has a separated s curve, a low o/n connection and a sharply raised terminal t. There is no separate i dot or extra e body in the clear space before that terminal, unlike the distinctly dotted soit higher on this page.
